Acts of Violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in Parigi Moutong Regency so that they are protected from Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence in the form of regional regulations. Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence have not regulated protection efforts at the Regional level, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation. This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of Women and Children Victims of Violence in Parigi Moutong Regency.

Part Two

Obligations and Responsibilities

Article 24

(1) The obligation and responsibility in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence is the shared responsibility of the Regional Government and the Community.

(2) The obligations and responsibilities of the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (1). include:

a. establishing, implementing policies, programs, and conducting cooperative activities in the provision of protection for women and children from acts of violence;

b. facilitating the establishment of institutional protection for women and children from acts of violence and providing support for facilities and infrastructure;

c. allocating budget for the provision of protection for women and children from acts of violence in accordance with the Regional financial capacity;

d. fostering and supervising the provision of protection for women and children from acts of violence;

e. providing protection services for women and children victims of acts of violence;

f. encouraging and increasing community participation; and

g. appointing parents and/or substitute family caregivers as a protective measure for children who are victims of acts of violence.

CHAPTER VII

COMMUNITY AND BUSINESS PARTICIPATION

Article 25

(1) Every person may participate in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence.

(2) Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by:

a. preventing and stopping the occurrence of acts of violence;

b. providing protection to victims;

c. providing first aid to victims of acts of violence;

d. reporting acts of violence against women and/or children;

e. independently socializing the rights of women and children;

f. strengthening community social institutions in handling acts of violence against women and children; and/or

g. disseminating information about laws and regulations relating to acts of violence against women and children.

Article 26

(1) The Regional Government encourages the business sector to participate in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.

(2) Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may take the form of:

a. socialization to employees within the company environment regarding the dangers of acts of violence against women and children; and

b. assistance as a form of corporate social responsibility.

Article 27

(1) The Regional Government prepares and develops an information and reporting system for the protection of women and children from acts of violence.

(2) The information and reporting system as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE I. GENERAL

Acts of Violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in Parigi Moutong Regency so that they are protected from Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence in the form of regional regulations. Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence have not regulated protection efforts at the Regional level, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation. This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of Women and Children Victims of Violence in Parigi Moutong Regency.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 4

Letter a What is meant by "physical violence" is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death.

Letterb What is meant by "sexual violence" is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.

Letter cWhat is meant by "economic violence" is an action that restricts a person from working inside or outside the home to earn money and goods, including allowing a person who works to be exploited, while someone does not fulfill the economic needs of the family.

Letter dWhat is meant by "social violence" is an act of a person or group of people that causes injury or loss of life of a person or may cause physical damage or damage to another person's property.

LetterеWhat is meant by "psychological violence" is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Letterf

What is meant by "Domestic Neglect" is: a. actions that result in the non-fulfillment of;

b. the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social;

c. actions of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or take care of children as they should be;

d. actions that neglect persons within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or covenant they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such persons;

e. actions that result in economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of such person.

a. the right to survival, growth and development; f"fl
b. the right to basic population services; rr
c. the right to equal protection;
d. the right to be free from various stigma; and
e. the right to obtain freedom.

a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and/or

b. other lawful sources that are non-binding in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

e. providing protection services for women and children victims of acts of violence;

f. encouraging and increasing community participation; and

g. appointing parents and/or substitute family caregivers as a protective measure for children who are victims of acts of violence.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE I. GENERAL

Acts of Violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in Parigi Moutong Regency so that they are protected from Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence in the form of regional regulations. Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence have not regulated protection efforts at the Regional level, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation. This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of Women and Children Victims of Violence in Parigi Moutong Regency.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE I. GENERAL

Acts of Violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in Parigi Moutong Regency so that they are protected from Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence in the form of regional regulations. Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence have not regulated protection efforts at the Regional level, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation. This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of Women and Children Victims of Violence in Parigi Moutong Regency.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Part Two

Obligations and Responsibilities

Article 24

(1) The obligation and responsibility in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence is the shared responsibility of the Regional Government and the Community.

(2) The obligations and responsibilities of the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (1). include:

a. establishing, implementing policies, programs, and conducting cooperative activities in the provision of protection for women and children from acts of violence;

b. facilitating the establishment of institutional protection for women and children from acts of violence and providing support for facilities and infrastructure;

c. allocating budget for the provision of protection for women and children from acts of violence in accordance with the Regional financial capacity;

d. fostering and supervising the provision of protection for women and children from acts of violence;

e. providing protection services for women and children victims of acts of violence;

f. encouraging and increasing community participation; and

g. appointing parents and/or substitute family caregivers as a protective measure for children who are victims of acts of violence.

CHAPTER VII

COMMUNITY AND BUSINESS PARTICIPATION

Article 25

(1) Every person may participate in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence.

(2) Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by:

a. preventing and stopping the occurrence of acts of violence;

b. providing protection to victims;

c. providing first aid to victims of acts of violence;

d. reporting acts of violence against women and/or children;

e. independently socializing the rights of women and children;

f. strengthening community social institutions in handling acts of violence against women and children; and/or

g. disseminating information about laws and regulations relating to acts of violence against women and children.

Article 26

(1) The Regional Government encourages the business sector to participate in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.

(2) Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may take the form of:

a. socialization to employees within the company environment regarding the dangers of acts of violence against women and children; and

b. assistance as a form of corporate social responsibility.

CHAPTER VIII

INFORMATION AND REPORTING SYSTEM

Article 27

(1) The Regional Government prepares and develops an information and reporting system for the protection of women and children from acts of violence.

(2) The information and reporting system as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 30

(1) The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations, or non-governmental organizations that carry out protection of women and children from acts of violence.

(2) Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with the Regional financial capacity and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 31

Protection activities for Women and Children Victims of Acts of Violence organized by P2TP2A before this Regional Regulation is promulgated, are declared to remain valid until the establishment of the Technical Implementation Unit of the Women and Child Protection Service by the Regional Government.

17. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for strengthening Violence Victims to resolve the problems they face.

18. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Children Victims of Violence to their families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.

19. 20. Rehabilitation is the recovery of Victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society.

21. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with families, communities, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.

22. Restitution is payment of compensation imposed on the perpetrator based on a court decision that has permanent legal force for material and/or immaterial losses suffered by the victim or their heirs.

23. Technical Implementation Unit of the Office for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is the Technical Implementation Unit of the Office for the Protection of Women and Children of Parigi Moutong Regency.

24. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an integrated service provider institution for Victims established by the Regional Government.

Minimum Service Standards, hereinafter abbreviated as SPM, are performance benchmarks for integrated service units in providing complaint handling services, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance as well as repatriation and social reintegration for Women and Children Victims of Violence.

26. Social Welfare Organization Institution, hereinafter referred to as LPKS, is an institution or social service facility that carries out the implementation of social welfare for Children in conflict with the law, established by the ministry of social affairs.

27. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to provide protection to Victims in accordance with predetermined standards.

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE I. GENERAL

Acts of Violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in Parigi Moutong Regency so that they are protected from Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence in the form of regional regulations. Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence have not regulated protection efforts at the Regional level, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation. This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of Women and Children Victims of Violence in Parigi Moutong Regency.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE I. GENERAL

Acts of Violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in Parigi Moutong Regency so that they are protected from Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence in the form of regional regulations. Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence have not regulated protection efforts at the Regional level, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation. This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of Women and Children Victims of Violence in Parigi Moutong Regency.

Article 24

(2) The obligations and responsibilities of the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (1). include:

e. providing protection services for women and children victims of acts of violence;

f. encouraging and increasing community participation; and

c. providing first aid to victims of acts of violence;

e. independently socializing the rights of women and children;

f. strengthening community social institutions in handling acts of violence against women and children; and/or

g. disseminating information about laws and regulations relating to acts of violence against women and children.

b. assistance as a form of corporate social responsibility.

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: ; 1. Region is the Regency of Parigi Moutong. I

2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the organizer of Regional Government who leads the implementation of government affairs which are the authority of the autonomous region. t

3. Regent is the Regent of Parigi Moutong.

4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives t

Region in the organization of Government affairs which are the authority of the Region.

5. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb.

6. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and organizations and Zatau community.

7. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and their children, or mother and their children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree.

8. Violence is any act that results in suffering or misery physically, psychologically, sexually, and I or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty;

9. Violence against Women is any action that results in or may result in suffering or misery of Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.

10. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in suffering or misery physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and mistreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child

11. Victim is Women and Children who experience suffering and or misery either directly or indirectly as a result of Violence.

12. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that Violence against Women will or has occurred;

13. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from Violence and discrimination.

14. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development.

15. Service is action taken as soon as possible to the Victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that Violence against the Victim will, is or has occurred.

16. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany Victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of Violence Victims.

17. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for strengthening Violence Victims to resolve the problems they face.

18. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Children Victims of Violence to their families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.

19. Counseling is a process of providing objective and complete information, carried out systematically with interpersonal communication guidance, guidance techniques and mastery of clinical knowledge aimed at helping someone recognize their current condition, the problems they are facing, and determine a solution or effort to overcome these problems. . .

20. Rehabilitation is the recovery of Victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society.

21. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with families, communities, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.

22. Restitution is payment of compensation imposed on the perpetrator based on a court decision that has permanent legal force for material and/or immaterial losses suffered by the victim or their heirs.

23. Technical Implementation Unit of the Office for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is the Technical Implementation Unit of the Office for the Protection of Women and Children of Parigi Moutong Regency.

24. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an integrated service provider institution for Victims established by the Regional Government.

25. Minimum Service Standards, hereinafter abbreviated as SPM, are performance benchmarks for integrated service units in providing complaint handling services, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance as well as repatriation and social reintegration for Women and Children Victims of Violence.

26. Social Welfare Organization Institution, hereinafter referred to as LPKS, is an institution or social service facility that carries out the implementation of social welfare for Children in conflict with the law, established by the ministry of social affairs.

27. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to provide protection to Victims in accordance with predetermined standards.

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE I. GENERAL

Acts of Violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in Parigi Moutong Regency so that they are protected from Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence in the form of regional regulations. Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence have not regulated protection efforts at the Regional level, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation. This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of Women and Children Victims of Violence in Parigi Moutong Regency.
